steps: Unpack & check contents
Lay every part on a clean, soft, dry surface and check it against the parts list. The unit has glass components — handle with extreme caution.

Package contents (Section 1.5):

  • Electric fireplace
  • Instruction manual
  • Remote control and batteries
  • Smoked crushed glass (boxed)
  • Glass suction clamp
  • Power cord
  • Log set
  • Mounting screw packet (QTY 4)

Tools (not included): Phillips screwdriver, stud finder, level, tape measure, electric drill, 1/4" wood drill bit.

Keep plastic packaging and small parts away from young children.
Plan location & power

Follow national and local building and electrical codes; pick a spot not prone to moisture, away from drapes, furniture and flammable vapors or liquids. Plan an electrical box for the supplied cord, or hardwire — required for a recessed installation.

• Location not susceptible to moisture; away from drapes and furniture.
  • Combustibles (curtains, drapes, furniture, bedding, paper) at least 36" (914mm) from the front (p. 16).
  • Don't store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids near the heater.
  • Supplied power cord: plan where it connects to an electrical box.
  • Recessed installation: must be hardwired. All work by a licensed electrician to local and national (NFPA 70) electrical codes.

Manufactured homes: meets H.U.D. construction and safety standards when installed per these instructions (p. 1).
Prep the sides for your option
Single-sided keeps both block-off plates, corner removes the one on the side to be visible, 3-sided (bay) removes both. Swap the side cover plates and "C" finishing trim to match.

Standard (single-sided)

On both sides: remove the screws holding the cover plate and finishing trim, discard the "C" finishing trim, then refit the cover plate and screws. Framing then sits flush with the appliance body and the finishing material butts against the 1/2" finishing edge.

Corner (left or right)

Side to be exposed: remove the cover plate screws, discard the cover plate, refit the finishing trim. Other side: remove the same screws, discard the finishing trim, refit the cover plate.

3-sided (bay)

Both sides: remove and discard the cover plate, then refit the "C" finishing trim with the same screws. All 3 sides of viewing glass are then exposed.

On exposed sides, the finishing trim is what your finishing material butts against.
Nailing flanges
Fold out the 2 top and 2 bottom nailing flanges (Fig. 2.5). They secure the appliance to the framing.
Frame the rough opening

Build the rough opening for your installation type (Fig. 2.6–2.8) and hold the Table 2.1 clearances. Once the unit is installed and secured in the opening, remove and discard the shipping support brace.

Standard

A64-3/4" (1645mm)
B23-1/2" (597mm)
C19-1/2" (495mm)

Corner

A63-3/4" (1619mm)
B23-1/2" (597mm)
C19-1/2" (495mm)

3-sided (bay)

A63" (1600mm)
B23-1/2" (597mm)
C19-1/2" (495mm)

A, B and C are as marked on the figures (pp. 16–18). Clearances: 0" bottom and sides, 1/4" (6mm) back and top, 36" (914mm) to combustibles in front of the glass (p. 15).

The shipping support brace comes off only after the unit is installed and secured in the framed opening (p. 12).
Optional surround or trim

Both fit only a recessed single-sided installation. The rectangle surround hangs on magnetic brackets with its deeper flange at the bottom; the 4-piece finishing trim goes on with the supplied double-sided adhesive tape.

Rectangle surround (OSX64-RS)

Recommended over an unfinished or exposed edge of drywall, tile or wood.

  1. Remove the 2 Phillips screws above the viewing glass and the heater air deflector bracket. Discard the bracket; save the screws.
  2. Install the new heater air deflector bracket (support flanges on the ends).
  3. Install the base brackets.
  4. Install the magnetic hanging brackets with the supplied screws; adjust them to your finishing material.
  5. Hang the top of the surround on the hanging brackets. The larger (deeper) flange goes at the bottom — at the top it may cover the heater vents.
  6. Hold the bottom with the provided magnets on the bottom edge of the fireplace, hidden by the bottom flange.

To remove it, pull the trim forward and up off the brackets.

4-piece finishing trim

Recommended for a smooth wall finish or very thin finishing materials. Install the top and bottom pieces, then the sides, with the supplied double-sided adhesive tape (p. 24).
Electrical connection

Remove the 4 electrical box cover screws, move the cable clamp to the side, top or rear (knock-out plate) if needed, complete the connection and refit the cover. A recessed installation must be hardwired by a licensed electrician (NFPA 70).

The appliance ships ready for either hardwiring or the supplied power cord; the cable clamp secures either.

  1. Remove the 4 screws that secure the electrical box cover (Fig. 2.17).
  2. Move the cable clamp to the desired location (Fig. 2.18). Cabling can also exit the top of the appliance through the cover plate.
  3. Complete the electrical connection and reinstall the electrical box cover.

Supply: 120VAC, 60Hz, 1500W; a dedicated 15 Amp (or higher) breaker is recommended (p. 9).
Finish the wall & mantel

Keep the combined wall projection, finishing material and combustible mantel within 12" (305mm), and nothing inside the finishing edges or over the glass. The finishing edges take material up to 1/2" (13mm) thick.

• All minimum clearances to combustible material must be maintained.
  • Wall bump-out: up to 12" (305mm) of projection, starting at the top finishing edge.
  • Combustible mantel projections must fall within that 12" (305mm) wall projection (Fig. 3.1).
  • No material may extend inside the finishing edges or block the viewing area or glass.
  • Finishing material thicker than 1/2" (13mm) leaves some of its edge exposed; on a single-sided install the optional rectangle surround covers it (p. 27).
Remove the glass

Front glass: suction cup on, remove the top right and left screws and brackets and the heater air deflector bracket, tilt toward you and lift out. Then the holographic pane: remove its 2 top-corner clips and lift it out of the bottom channel.

Glass front (Section 4.1)

  1. Remove any front trim, if installed.
  2. Attach a glass suction cup. Remove the screws and brackets at the top right and left of the glass, and the heater air deflector bracket. Save them.
  3. Tilt the glass toward you, lift it up and out, and lay it face down on a soft, non-abrasive surface.

Holographic glass (Section 4.2)

  1. Attach the suction cup to the holographic pane and remove the 2 glass panel clips, one in each top corner.
  2. Tilt it up slightly, lift it up and out of the bottom glass channel, and set it on a soft, non-abrasive surface.
  3. Note which side faced up: that side has a reflective film and must face up again.

Reinstall in reverse order, then refit any front trim.

Don't rely on the suction cups to carry the weight of the glass — they are only for tilting it back. Wear safety gloves and glasses (p. 36).
Install the x64 log set

Match each log to the numbered position on the clear floor panel, plugging the LED-lit logs into the floor connector beside them. Finish with the 20 lbs. of crushed glass and klinkers, kept back from the front edge.

1. Base logs: #1, #2, #14, #9 and #6.
  2. Back row, LED-lit — plug each into the female connector in the plastic floor next to its position: #3 first, then #7, #4, #5 and #8.
  3. Front row: #10, #11, #12, #13 and #15. Logs #11, #13 and #15 are LED-lit; plug them in.
  4. Add the 20 lbs. of crushed glass and klinkers. Space the klinkers randomly on top; use them to hide the log wires.
Keep the crushed glass back from the very front edge — the angled holographic glass needs space there.

The log LED connection is shown on p. 31; the x64 log positions on p. 32.

on.title: Turning it on and off
on.html:
You can run the fireplace from the control panel on the fireplace or from the remote. The fire and the heater have separate buttons.

  1. On the control panel, push the main power switch to I. The main power indicator lights up.
  2. Press Fireplace On/Off on the panel, or on/off on the remote, to turn the fire on or off.
  3. Want heat as well? Turn the heater on too — see Heat & thermostat.
The remote can only turn the fireplace on when the main power switch on the control panel is on.

Shutting it down completely

To disconnect it fully, turn the controls off, then turn off the power to its circuit at your main electrical panel.

Before the first use, the fireplace must be properly installed. Read the whole manual, including the safety information, before you plug it in or use it.

heat.title: Heat settings & thermostat
heat.html:
The heater has its own buttons, separate from the fire. It has two settings.

Half heat750W
Full heat1500W

On the control panel

Press Heater once for half heat. Press it again for full heat. A third press turns the heater off.

On the remote

  • Heater On/Off turns the heater on or off.
  • Press Heater once for half power, a second time for full power.
  • Temperature Set steps through 8 preset temperatures.
  • Timer steps through 8 timer settings.

The remote works as the thermostat. Its temperature sensor tells the fireplace the room temperature, so keep it in the same room, screen up, sensor uncovered, and away from the fireplace front or a warm window.

To switch between Fahrenheit and Celsius, press and hold Down Light on the control panel for 3 seconds, until it beeps.

This heater is for supplemental heat only. It isn't meant to be your main heat source.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
Your remote comes already paired with the fireplace. The main power switch on the fireplace's control panel must be on for the remote to turn it on.

Where to keep it

  • In the same room as the fireplace, with the remote's screen facing up.
  • With its temperature sensor uncovered.
  • Not next to the front of the fireplace or in a warm spot such as a window. False temperature readings stop the fireplace turning on and off accurately with the room temperature.

Batteries

When the battery indicator on the remote shows empty, replace its 2 AAA batteries with the correct type (1.5V AAA). Make sure they go in the right way round.

Pairing a new remote

  1. Turn the main power switch on.
  2. Press and hold fireplace on/off and Display Brightness at the same time for 5 seconds.
  3. You'll hear beeping. When it stops, the remote is paired.

To clear the app pairing so you can re-pair the app, press and hold Floor Light on the control panel for 3 seconds, until it beeps.

effects.title: Flames, lights & sound
effects.html:
Each of these remote buttons steps through its options. Keep pressing to cycle round.

Flame Color7 colors
Flame Effect4 effects
Floor LED Colors13 colors
Down Light3 options
Log Light Brightness3 levels
Display Brightness5 levels

Night mode

Night mode turns off all the lights except the log lights. Press the night mode button to go in and out of it.

Crackling sound

Press sound to turn the crackling sound on or off.

On the fireplace itself

The control panel's Down Light button cycles through 3 colors, and its Floor Light button through 13 colors.

sounds.title: Those beeps and smells are normal
sounds.html:
Beeps

The control panel beeps every time you press one of its buttons. That just tells you the press worked. Holding a panel button for 3 seconds, to switch °F/°C or clear the app pairing, also ends with a beep.

You'll hear beeping while a new remote pairs. When it stops, pairing is done.

Crackling

The crackling is a sound effect. Turn it on or off with the sound button on the remote.

A slight smell at first

A slight odor the first time you turn the fireplace on is normal. It shouldn't come back unless the fireplace goes unused for a long time.

If it ever malfunctions, stop using it. Turn off the power at the service panel and have an authorized Kozy Heat dealer inspect it before you use it again.

clean.title: Cleaning the fireplace
clean.html:
Dust, lint and pet hair in the air vents are a fire risk, so keep the air inlet and heater area clean.

First, turn off the power

Make sure the toggle switch on the control panel is off. Then disconnect the power: unplug the fireplace, or turn off its circuit at the main electrical panel.

Vents and heater area

  • Before use, check the air vents for dust, lint or anything blocking them.
  • Clean the air inlet and heater area regularly to keep them free of dust and pet hair.
Note: p. 7 says to clean the vents with a vacuum only; p. 36 says to clean the air inlet and heater area with a cloth or vacuum.

What to avoid

  • Don't use abrasive cleaners.
  • Don't spray liquids directly onto the fireplace.
  • Don't rinse it or let it get wet.

For the glass, see Clean the glass.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
1. Turn the power off first, as for any cleaning.
  2. Spray glass cleaner onto a cloth, not onto the glass.
  3. Wipe the glass, then dry it with a lint-free cloth.
Handle with care. The glass is tempered for safety, and a hard impact will shatter it. Take extra care that a corner of the glass never hits a hard surface.

If you take the glass out to clean it

  • Wear safety gloves and safety glasses.
  • Lay the glass on a soft surface.
  • Don't carry it by the suction cups. They're only there to tilt the glass back so it can come out.
  • A holographic glass pane comes out after the front glass. Note which side faced up: that side has a reflective film, and it must go back the same way up.

The removal steps for both panes are on pages 29 and 30 of the manual.

safety.title: Safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
• The heater is hot when in use. Don't let bare skin touch hot surfaces.
  • Keep furniture, pillows, bedding, papers, clothes and curtains at least 36" (914mm) from the front.
  • Take extreme care when children or vulnerable adults are near it, and whenever you leave it running unattended.
  • Don't block the air intakes or exhaust, and don't let anything get into the vents. That can cause an electric shock, a fire or damage.
  • It has hot, arcing or sparking parts inside. Don't use it where gasoline, paint or other flammable vapors or liquids are used or stored.
  • Indoors only. Don't use it outdoors, and don't let it get wet.
  • Don't tamper with any controls.
  • Keep plastic packaging and small parts away from young children.
After a malfunction, don't operate it. Turn off the power at the service panel and have an authorized Kozy Heat dealer inspect it before you use it again.

outlet.title: Plug & outlet safety
outlet.html:
This heater draws more current than other small heaters. Overheating may happen even if it never did with other heaters.

  • Always plug the power cord directly into a wall outlet.
  • Never use an extension cord or a power strip.
  • Never use an outlet that's old, cracked, or has loose wires or connections. A faulty outlet can arc, overheat or catch fire.
  • Check that the plug fits tight in the outlet. A loose plug can make the outlet overheat.

Your fireplace may be hardwired (connected straight into your home's wiring) instead of plugged in. A recessed installation must be hardwired, by a licensed electrician.

A dedicated 15 Amp (or higher) breaker is recommended. The 1500W heater can draw 12.5 amps.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Note: the manual gives the warranty term as "Limited Lifetime Warranty" in the title on p. 5 and p. 40, and as "2 Year Limited Warranty" (all parts for 2 years, labor reimbursement for 1 year) in the coverage on p. 40.

It covers defects in materials and workmanship, for the original purchaser only. It can't be transferred.

Parts2 years
Labor reimbursement1 year, to an authorized dealer only

Coverage starts on the date of original purchase. For new home construction, it starts at first occupancy or six months after the dealer's sale, whichever comes first. Nothing needs to be sent in to register. Keep your dated proof of purchase with the serial number and model.

Not covered, or voids it

  • Not bought through an authorized Kozy Heat dealer or distributor.
  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual.
  • Wear items: paint, batteries and glass discoloration.
  • Damp places, weather or water damage, such as outdoors, porches or laundry rooms.
  • Power interruptions or fluctuations, misuse, or unapproved parts or changes.
  • How well it heats your space.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Rating120VAC, 60Hz, 1500W
Heater draw12.5 amps
BreakerDedicated 15 Amp (or higher), recommended
Cord3-prong, supplied

Cord: two flat blades (live and neutral) and one round pin (ground). Ships for either hardwiring or the supplied cord. A recessed installation must be hardwired — licensed electrician, local and national (NFPA 70) electrical codes. The cable clamp moves to the side, top or rear via a knock-out plate (p. 25).

If a 3-slot receptacle is not available, an adapter (not included) must be used, with its green grounding lug connected to a permanent ground such as a properly grounded outlet box. Don't use the adapter if a three-slot grounded receptacle is available. Separately, p. 7 says always plug directly into a wall outlet — never an extension cord or power tap (outlet/power strip).

Listed by Intertek Testing Services: CSA C22.2 No 46-13 Ed.9 Electric Air-Heaters (R2018); UL 2021:2015 (4th Edition + R:02 Fed. 2021) Fixed and Location-Dedicated Electric Room Heaters. Meets H.U.D. construction and safety standards for manufactured homes when installed per these instructions (p. 1).

conflicts.issue: Warranty term: titled 'Limited Lifetime Warranty' in the contents (p. 5) and the page heading (p. 40), but the coverage text on p. 40 says '2 Year Limited Warranty' — all parts 2 years, labor reimbursement 1 year (exclusions also refer to the 24 month warranty period).

review.notes: One manual (Rev. 4, July 2026) covers OSO-x50 and OSO-x64; only x64 values are used. No troubleshooting chart or code table in the manual, so faults is null and codes is empty. Catalog checks: 1500 W and the 36" front clearance match (pp. 9, 15); the manual gives no weight, BTU/hr or view-area figure, so 291 lb, 5,000 BTU and 15-7/8" x 63" could not be checked. The catalog features' 'adjustable flame height and speed' is not described anywhere in the manual (remote offers flame color x7 and flame effect x4 only). Dimension letters A-H (Fig. 1.1) and framing letters A-C (Figs. 2.6-2.8) are not named in the text, so the guide shows them as letters. 'Recessed installation' (must be hardwired) is not defined against the other framed installs. p. 9 says a grounding adapter must be used where no 3-slot receptacle exists, while p. 7 says always plug directly into a wall outlet (no extension cord or power tap) — both shown in specElec, not flagged as a conflict. p. 36 says power off via the control-panel toggle switch for maintenance; p. 7 says disconnect from the power supply / unplug — the owner drawer gives both. The pairing buttons ('fireplace on/off' + 'Display Brightness') are not said to be on the remote or the panel, so the guide doesn't say. An app is mentioned only for clearing its pairing (Floor Light, 3 s); no app setup is described. Text quirks: p. 19 footer reads 'Rev. 7 - July 2025' with OSE serial numbers, unlike every other page; p. 16 says '3-Sided Pier' where elsewhere it is '3-Sided (Bay)'; Figure 4.4 is used twice (log LED connection p. 31, x64 log positions p. 32); back clearance printed 1/4"" (6mm); p. 36 says the glass is 'temperature for safety' (rendered as tempered). Install steps follow the manual's section order (2.4 nailing flanges precedes 2.6 framing; brace removal noted at framing per 2.3.1).
